goal: Barkdown runs its library without a source checkout or an Elixir toolchain on the machine: the runtime is a packaged release, and step by step the rest of what an installation needs.
scope: A profile's runtime from a packaged Barkpark release, built and stamped by a script
The portable profile, crash reclaim and recovery unchanged on the packaged runtime
The app itself as a macOS application that carries its runtime
acceptance: With only system folders on the PATH the app boots a profile's runtime, writes, restarts and reads the same
Export, import and reclaim after a kill pass on the packaged runtime
A machine with no Postgres installed runs a profile
A built macOS application starts a profile with nothing else installed
nextAction: 1) Postgres without a machine install: carry the server binaries beside the release and point the driver at them; rehearse with Homebrew's Postgres hidden. 2) Build the macOS application with the runtime inside and start a profile from it. 3) Settings: choose a packaged runtime for a new profile without typing a path.
truthReview: 2026-09-30: one Electron rehearsal on macOS runs a profile on a release built on the same machine, with only system folders on the app's PATH: first boot, a note written and read after a restart, export and import, reclaim after a kill. Postgres is still the machine's own. The app runs from source. Windows is not covered: the upstream release is assembled for unix hosts only.
screenshotReview: No renderer change. One live screenshot of a note on the packaged runtime is in the rehearsal folder.

remaining: A built macOS application that carries the runtime
Choosing a packaged runtime in Settings
Windows: no upstream release for that host
